description: Single-call replacement for the beacon → mechanical_evaluation → roll_qualifier chain. The model decides whether the player's intent needs a roll and emits ONE roll spec (or 'no roll'), plus the cross-cutting signals downstream code consumed from the old chain (affected_contexts, expand_scene, transition, combatants).

fields.needs_roll: boolean — true if a die roll is required to resolve this intent, false otherwise.
fields.no_roll_reason: string or null — short factual reason when needs_roll is false (e.g. 'walking down a hallway requires no check'). Required when needs_roll is false. Leave null when needs_roll is true.
fields.roll: object or null — the single roll request when needs_roll is true; null otherwise. Shape: { type ('skill_check'|'saving_throw'|'attack_roll'|'other'), skill (PF1e skill name e.g. 'Climb', 'Diplomacy' — required for skill_check), save ('fort'|'ref'|'will' — required for saving_throw), dc (integer; the rule-defined DC), description (one short sentence the player will see), take_10_eligible (boolean — true when no immediate threat or distraction), take_20_eligible (boolean — true when the action can be retried freely with no failure penalty), situational_modifiers (array of { source: string, modifier: integer } — empty when none), rule_slug (the slug of the rule from RELEVANT RULES that supports this DC, for audit) }.
fields.affected_domains: array of strings — which of {combat, traversal, social, exploration, rest, inventory, buff} this action touches. Drives downstream context updates and Chronicler routing. Empty array when the action has no in-world effect.
fields.expand_scene: boolean — true when the social interaction depends on facts the player CANNOT KNOW WITHOUT TALKING TO THE NPC, so a single skill check would wave away the actual interaction. Examples: 'I rent a room' (does the inn have rooms? are any vacant? what's the price? who runs it? — none of that is answerable by a Diplomacy roll), 'I ask the merchant about the cult' (does she know anything? will she share? at what cost?), 'I try to hire a guide' (is anyone available? trustworthy?). Setting this true triggers a dedicated social scene that establishes the NPC, surfaces constraints, and ends at the player's next decision (which may then trigger a follow-up roll). Only valid when 'social' is in affected_domains AND no active social interaction is already running in RECENT NARRATIVE BEATS. See expand_scene-vs-needs_roll guidance below.
fields.transition: string or null — set to 'combat_started' when the player's action initiates combat with hostile creatures. Otherwise null. Do NOT use this field to end combat; combat-end is handled by the combat path.
fields.combatants: array — required and non-empty when transition == 'combat_started'. Each entry is either a string ('goblin') or a one-key object ({ 'goblin': 3 }) for groups. Use exact creature names that would appear in a Pathfinder 1e bestiary.
fields.destination: string or null — when the action involves traveling, the destination location name; null otherwise.
fields.consequences: array of strings — automatic consequences of the action that don't require a roll (e.g. 'door is now open', 'lantern lit'). Empty when none.
fields.ability_use_claimed: string or null — name of a spell, feat, or item the player explicitly invoked (e.g. 'Fireball', 'Power Attack', 'potion of healing'). Code validates against the character sheet; do not invent.
fields.mechanical_summary: string — one-sentence factual summary of what this action does mechanically. Used by the post-roll arbitration step. When needs_roll is false, summarize the auto-resolution.
fields.reasoning: string — one short sentence explaining your call (which rule applied, why no roll, etc.). For audit only.

notes: Single-roll scope: the upstream Sequencer has already split compound actions, so this call resolves exactly one mechanical action. If the intent legitimately needs more than one roll, pick the primary roll and let downstream pipelines pick up follow-ups.

expand_scene vs needs_roll: pick at most one. expand_scene exists so we don't wave away interactions that depend on unknowns the player can only discover through dialogue (does the service exist, is the NPC willing, what are the terms). needs_roll is for a defined tactic against a known situation with a clear DC. If you cannot point to the specific NPC the roll targets and the specific outcome a success would produce — because those facts haven't been established yet — expand_scene is the right call. If the NPC, the stakes, and the asked-for outcome are already known and the player is now applying a tactic, request the roll.
DC selection: use rule-defined DCs from RELEVANT RULES. If no rule clearly applies, prefer needs_roll=false with a no_roll_reason rather than inventing a DC.

Take 10/20: take_10 is allowed when there is no immediate threat or distraction. take_20 is allowed when the action can be repeated freely with no penalty for failure (e.g. searching a room out of combat).
No roll for routine actions: walking, looking around, talking to friendly NPCs, drinking from a waterskin — these are needs_roll=false unless a specific rule from RELEVANT RULES says otherwise.
No character sheet visibility: skill modifiers, attack bonuses, save bonuses, spell lists are NOT in your prompt. Identify the kind of check; code resolves the actual modifier from the sheet.
